meta.description: This catalog enumerates every reasoning-trail shape classifyEncounter() can produce, for design reference.
meta.note: All `text` values below are byte-verbatim copies of literal strings in classify-encounter.ts -- there is no runtime string templating in this engine, only the `facts` object varies numerically/categorically per invocation. Where a trail entry's text has more than one literal variant reachable within the same shape (Rule 7's risk/no-risk pair), `text` is an object keyed by the condition instead of a plain string; every value inside that object is still a verbatim literal from the source.

stage0Failures.description: Propagated unchanged from relativeBearing() (via bearing()) when the two vessels occupy the same position. classifyEncounter() returns this Result failure before pushing anything to trail -- no trail is ever built.

Propagated unchanged from relativeBearing()/cpa() when a non-finite numeric field (position, heading, or speed) is detected. classifyEncounter() returns this Result failure before pushing anything to trail -- no trail is ever built.

reasoningTrails.summary: previous encounter type was 'overtaking' and Rule 7's risk-of-collision gate still holds, so the classification stays overtaking via hysteresis without re-testing the 112.5 degree boundary.
reasoningTrails.giveWay: vesselB when |relativeBearingAtoB| >= |relativeBearingBtoA|, otherwise vesselA (direction tie-break, not a distinct trail-text shape)
reasoningTrails.standOn: the vessel not selected by the giveWay tie-break above

trail.text: Risk of collision exists: the vessels are closing (positive TCPA) with a projected closest-approach distance at or under the 1.0nm threshold.
Overtaking situation persists (once overtaking, always overtaking until finally past and clear) -- previous classification was overtaking and Rule 7 risk of collision still holds.
Rule 18 does not apply to an overtaking situation: Rule 13(a) overrides Rules 4-18, so the overtaking vessel gives way regardless of vessel type.

reasoningTrails.summary: Fresh dispatch (no sticky hysteresis in effect): bearing from A to B exceeds 112.5 degrees abaft A's beam, so vessel B is overtaking vessel A.

text.whenRiskOfCollision: Risk of collision exists: the vessels are closing (positive TCPA) with a projected closest-approach distance at or under the 1.0nm threshold.
text.whenNoRisk: No risk of collision: either the vessels are not closing, closest approach already occurred, or the projected closest-approach distance exceeds the 1.0nm threshold.

trail.text: Vessel B is overtaking Vessel A (bearing from A to B is more than 22.5 degrees abaft A's beam).
Rule 18 does not apply to an overtaking situation: Rule 13(a) overrides Rules 4-18, so the overtaking vessel gives way regardless of vessel type.

reasoningTrails.summary: Fresh dispatch where bearing from B to A exceeds 112.5 degrees abaft B's beam (aOvertakesB true, or the WR-02 both-true tie-break resolved the other way), so vessel A is overtaking vessel B.

text.whenRiskOfCollision: Risk of collision exists: the vessels are closing (positive TCPA) with a projected closest-approach distance at or under the 1.0nm threshold.
text.whenNoRisk: No risk of collision: either the vessels are not closing, closest approach already occurred, or the projected closest-approach distance exceeds the 1.0nm threshold.

trail.text: Vessel A is overtaking Vessel B (bearing from B to A is more than 22.5 degrees abaft B's beam).
Rule 18 does not apply to an overtaking situation: Rule 13(a) overrides Rules 4-18, so the overtaking vessel gives way regardless of vessel type.

reasoningTrails.summary: Not overtaking, both relative bearings are within +/-5 degrees (head-on sector), and the two vessels' Rule 18 priority tiers differ, so the lower-priority vessel type is assigned give-way.
reasoningTrails.giveWay: the vessel whose type has the higher PRIORITY number (lower real-world priority) per vesselPriority() -- populated at Stage 6, not null
reasoningTrails.standOn: the other vessel (the one with the lower PRIORITY number / higher real-world priority)

text.whenRiskOfCollision: Risk of collision exists: the vessels are closing (positive TCPA) with a projected closest-approach distance at or under the 1.0nm threshold.
text.whenNoRisk: No risk of collision: either the vessels are not closing, closest approach already occurred, or the projected closest-approach distance exceeds the 1.0nm threshold.

trail.text: Not overtaking in either direction -- both relative bearings are forward of the 112.5 degree abaft-the-beam threshold.
Head-on: the vessels are meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses, each seeing the other ahead or nearly ahead.
Rule 18 hierarchy applies even to a head-on encounter: the lower-priority vessel type must give way.

reasoningTrails.summary: Not overtaking, both relative bearings are within +/-5 degrees (head-on sector), and the two vessels' Rule 18 priority tiers are equal (including the not-under-command/restricted-in-ability-to-maneuver tie), so no give-way/stand-on is assigned -- mutual obligation stands.

text.whenRiskOfCollision: Risk of collision exists: the vessels are closing (positive TCPA) with a projected closest-approach distance at or under the 1.0nm threshold.
text.whenNoRisk: No risk of collision: either the vessels are not closing, closest approach already occurred, or the projected closest-approach distance exceeds the 1.0nm threshold.

trail.text: Not overtaking in either direction -- both relative bearings are forward of the 112.5 degree abaft-the-beam threshold.
Head-on: the vessels are meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses, each seeing the other ahead or nearly ahead.
Rule 18 does not apply: both vessels share the same priority tier (including the not-under-command/restricted-in-ability-to-maneuver tie) -- mutual obligation stands, no give-way/stand-on assigned.

reasoningTrails.summary: Not overtaking, not head-on (residual Rule 15 crossing), and the geometric give-way vessel's type outranks the geometric stand-on vessel's type in the Rule 18 hierarchy, so the verdict is flipped.
reasoningTrails.giveWay: the geometric baseline's stand-on label, swapped by the Rule 18 override (i.e. the vessel whose type outranks the other's)
reasoningTrails.standOn: the geometric baseline's give-way label, swapped by the Rule 18 override

trail.text: Not overtaking in either direction -- both relative bearings are forward of the 112.5 degree abaft-the-beam threshold.
Not head-on -- at least one vessel does not see the other ahead or nearly ahead.
Crossing: the vessel that has the other on her own starboard side must keep out of the way.
Rule 18 override: the geometric give-way vessel outranks the geometric stand-on vessel in the Rule 18 hierarchy -- verdict flipped.

reasoningTrails.summary: Same dispatch path as crossing-rule18-override, but the geometric give-way vessel's type does not outrank the stand-on vessel's type, so the geometric baseline stands unmodified.
reasoningTrails.giveWay: vesselA if relativeBearingAtoB > 0, otherwise vesselB (geometric baseline)
reasoningTrails.standOn: the other vessel from the geometric baseline
